subject: Medivista — eval delivery playbook, dataset format & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medivista.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Medivista — eval delivery playbook, dataset format & next steps

Hi Laura — great to speak earlier. Short recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before we start the customer-specific eval run on Redwood.

Quick recap of the call:
- Goal: validate model fit for Medivista triage assistant across three use cases (symptom intake, routing, and patient education).
- Success criteria: routing precision >= 92% and no regressions on safety prompts; user-facing fluency judged acceptable by clinical SME.
- Timeline: pilot eval run target: 2 weeks after we receive dataset + labels.

What we recommend from Redwood for initial runs:
- Models to test: 
  1) rw/open-7b-quant (fast baseline, cost-efficient)
  2) rw/opt-13b-8bit (balanced cost/quality)
  3) rw/llama-2-70b-hf (quality upper bound; will run on Dedicated capacity)
- Inference profile: streaming enabled for UI tests, KV-prefix caching for repeated triage forms, and int8 quantization for opt-13b where possible.

Deliverables we need from Medivista to start the eval:
1) A 2k sample CSV of real (anonymized) triage transcripts with columns: id, prompt, context, expected_label, confidence_threshold, notes. See filename sample attached.
2) A small gold-set of 200 manually-labeled cases (high-quality labels across edge cases).
3) Any blacklisted/unsafe prompt examples you want us to treat as failure cases.

Suggested scoring rubric (we can refine):
- Routing accuracy (macro-accuracy per intent) — primary metric
- Safety regressions count (explicit fails flagged by rules) — blocker if > 2% on gold-set
- Answer quality (2-point pass/fail by SME on 200-case gold set)
- Latency p95 under Dedicated target (for 70b) — < 500ms token generation for UI flows

Next steps / who does what:
- Laura / Medivista: upload sample dataset + gold-set to the S3 bucket we gave you (s3://redwood-evals/medivista/20261121) by Tue Nov 24.
- Aditya: configure the eval harness and share scoring template; schedule run on Dedicated if you opt for 70b.
- Marissa: will scope compute and attach cost estimate for the three-model sweep.

Attachments: medivista_sample_dataset_v1.zip (schema + dummy rows), redwood_eval_scoring_template.xlsx

If this all looks good I’ll open the HubSpot milestone and schedule the first run. Thanks again — excited to get hands-on.

Cheers,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — this is very clear and aligns with our expectations. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Gold-set labeling: we can deliver the 200-case gold-set but want to be explicit about label schema. For routing we have a three-level taxonomy (intents -> sub-intents -> escalation flag). Is Redwood able to score at the sub-intent level and surface confusion matrices?

2) Data sensitivity: the sample will be de-identified but contains free-text. Do you have recommended redaction best practices besides removing names and MRNs? Any automated PII scrub you recommend before upload?

3) Timing: Nov 24 is tight because our data team has a calendar freeze on the 24th. Would Nov 25 be okay for you?

We can upload the sample to the provided S3 path and will attach a short README with the taxonomy mapping.

—Laura
Head of Product, Medivista

Laura — thanks for the quick replies and the taxonomy note. A few operational clarifications from the ops side (so you know what we will run and how we will report):

Dataset format checklist (what we will validate before running):
- File: CSV or newline-delimited JSON (we prefer NDJSON for complex context fields).
- Required columns/keys: id, prompt, context, expected_label, label_granularity (intent|sub-intent), source, anonymized_flag.
- Context: include preceding 2 turns where available (we will truncate at 2048 tokens unless you ask otherwise).
- Label encoding: provide a mapping file (taxonomy.csv) with canonical intent IDs.

Scoring pipeline and outputs:
- We'll compute per-model metrics: routing macro-accuracy, sub-intent F1, top-3 intent recall, and a safety-fail count (rule-based checks on outputs).
- Confusion matrices: yes, we will output per-intent confusion matrices and a delta table that highlights regressions vs. baseline model.
- Regression guardrails: we will flag any model where safety-fail increase > 0.5 percentage points vs baseline or routing accuracy drops > 1.5 points on the gold-set.
- SME review: deliverable will include a 200-case SME sheet with pass/fail columns and free-text notes for failure cases.

PII & redaction guidance:
- Prefer client-side redaction on PII categories (names, full dates of birth, MRNs). We can also run a sanitized PII scrub on the Corpus export but recommend doing the first pass locally to avoid accidental PHI transfer.

Cost and compute: Ben will attach a cost estimate; rough numbers by profile: rw/open-7b-quant (low), rw/opt-13b-8bit (mid), rw/llama-2-70b (high; Dedicated commit recommended).

Operational question: Laura, if you upload Nov 25 we will validate on the 25th and aim to start the sweep on Nov 27, results out by Dec 3. Does that schedule work?

—Marissa
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference
